backlog.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same rdFingerprintGenerator generator, keeping radius 2 and 2048 bits. Counts of each substructure carry more information than presence bits. Leave the RandomForest settings and fit_predict logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the full RDKit descriptor set (Descriptors.descList, via rdkit.Chem.Descriptors) for each molecule, replace NaN and inf values with 0, clip extreme values to the 1st-99th percentile of the training set, and concatenate them with the Morgan bit vector before fitting the RandomForest. Blood-brain barrier penetration is driven by physicochemical properties such as polar surface area, MW and logP, so these features should help.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Build a compact feature vector of about 10 known BBB-relevant properties: TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, fraction of sp3 carbons, formal charge, count of carboxylic acid groups, and count of basic amines. Use it alone with a RandomForest, then compare against the fingerprint model in a later job. Small feature sets are less prone to overfitting when test skeletons are unseen.
backlog.title: Small curated BBB-heuristic feature set

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan featurizer with 166-bit MACCS structural keys from rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to a numpy array. MACCS keys are a coarser, pharmacophore-like encoding and generalize differently across scaffolds. Keep the RandomForest unchanged.
backlog.title: MACCS keys instead of Morgan

backlog.spec: Build the feature matrix by hstacking three blocks: the 2048-bit Morgan count fingerprint (radius 2), the 167-bit MACCS keys, and the RDKit 2D descriptors with NaN set to 0 and values clipped to training percentiles. Fit the same RandomForest on the combined matrix. This is a broader representation aimed at reducing scaffold-specific errors.
backlog.title: Concatenate Morgan, MACCS and descriptors

backlog.spec: Use the feature-invariant Morgan generator (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariants from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()) to produce functional-class fingerprints with radius 2 and 2048 bits, as counts. Functional-class features abstract away atom identity and can transfer better to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Feature-count-based FCFP fingerprint

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan featurizer with hashed atom-pair count fingerprints from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, using 2048 bits. Atom pairs encode topological distances between atoms and are complementary to circular fingerprints. Keep the RandomForest settings the same.
backlog.title: Atom-pair fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the featurizer with hashed topological torsion count fingerprints from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, 2048 bits. Torsion fingerprints capture longer-range chain patterns. Keep the RandomForest unchanged so only the representation changes.
backlog.title: Topological torsion fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForestClassifier with LightGBMClassifier using about 400 estimators, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, and random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Gradient boosting often beats random forests on tabular fingerprint data. Keep the Morgan featurizer.
backlog.title: Switch the RandomForest to LightGBM

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with XGBClassifier: 500 estimators, max_depth 5, learning_rate 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 2, eval_metric logloss, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Keep the Morgan 2048-bit featurizer. Boosted trees with column subsampling are a strong default for sparse binary features.
backlog.title: XGBoost classifier on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with CatBoostClassifier: 800 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, l2_leaf_reg 5, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8. Keep the Morgan featurizer. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees resist overfitting on small datasets like this one.
backlog.title: CatBoost on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the binary Morgan fingerprints (2048 bits). Build the Tanimoto similarity kernel K(a,b) = sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)) using numpy broadcasting on the bit matrices, in chunks if needed for memory. Train sklearn SVC with kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, probability=True, random_state=seed on the train-train kernel and predict using the test-train kernel. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for molecular property prediction.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVM

backlog.spec: Compute binary Morgan fingerprints (2048 bits, radius 2). For each test molecule, compute the Tanimoto similarity to all training molecules, take the k=10 most similar training molecules, and return a similarity-weighted mean of their labels (weights = similarity to the power 3). Fall back to the training base rate if all similarities are zero. This is a simple, nonparametric baseline that often works well for scaffold-split data.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbour Tanimoto classifier

backlog.spec: Build features from the Morgan count fingerprint and standardized RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN to 0, clipped to training percentiles). Fit sklearn LogisticRegression with penalty l2, C=0.1, max_iter=2000, class_weight='balanced'. Linear models are less likely to memorize scaffold-specific structure and may generalize better to unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Logistic regression on fingerprints plus descriptors

backlog.spec: Use the binary Morgan fingerprint (2048 bits) as input to sklearn MLPClassifier with hidden_layer_sizes=(512, 128), activation relu, alpha=1e-3 for L2 regularization, learning_rate_init 1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.1, max_iter 300, random_state=seed. Return predict_proba for class 1. Neural networks trained on fingerprints are a standard alternative to tree models.
backlog.title: Multilayer perceptron on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Train three models on the same Morgan fingerprint features: the existing RandomForest, a LightGBM classifier with 300 trees and learning_rate 0.05, and a logistic regression with C=0.5 on standardized features. Average their predicted probabilities with equal weights and return the mean. Diverse model families usually reduce variance on new scaffolds.
backlog.title: Soft-voting ensemble of RF, LightGBM and logistic regression

backlog.spec: Train the same RandomForest separately on three representations: Morgan radius-2 bits, atom-pair counts and MACCS keys. For each, convert the predicted probabilities on the test set into ranks, then average the three rank vectors and rescale to [0,1]. Rank averaging is robust to differences in probability calibration between the models.
backlog.title: Rank-averaged ensemble across fingerprint types

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, run 5-fold StratifiedKFold (seeded) on the training set to produce out-of-fold probabilities from a RandomForest on Morgan bits and from a LightGBM on the same bits. Fit a LogisticRegression on the two OOF probability columns, then refit both base models on the full training set and apply the meta-learner to their test probabilities. Stacking can learn how much to trust each base model.
backlog.title: Stacking with a logistic-regression meta-learner

backlog.spec: Keep the RandomForest and Morgan featurizer but set class_weight='balanced_subsample' in RandomForestClassifier. The BBBP labels are imbalanced toward the positive class, so reweighting can change which molecules are ranked high and improve AUROC on the minority class. No other changes.
backlog.title: Class-weighted random forest

backlog.spec: Set min_samples_leaf=3 and max_depth=None in RandomForestClassifier while keeping the other settings. Larger leaves smooth the predicted probabilities, which helps the AUROC ranking on unseen skeletons. Also set max_features='sqrt' to decorrelate the trees further.
backlog.title: Stronger leaf regularization in the forest

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES to 800 and set MAX_FEATURES to 0.1 (roughly sqrt of the 2048 bits, about 45 features), keeping all other settings. More trees reduce variance of the probability estimates, and a smaller feature fraction increases tree diversity. This is a plain hyperparameter change.
backlog.title: Tune the forest size and feature fraction

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, keep only the Morgan bits that are set in at least 2 training molecules and at most 98 percent of them, which removes near-constant bits. Compute this mask on the training fold only and apply it to both train and test features. Less noisy inputs reduce the chance that the forest splits on spurious rare substructures.
backlog.title: Bit-level feature selection before fitting

backlog.spec: In featurize, before computing fingerprints, parse each SMILES and keep only the largest connected fragment using rdkit.Chem.rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser (or by splitting on '.' and keeping the longest piece by heavy-atom count). Also neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Counterions and salts in the SMILES otherwise pollute the fingerprint.
backlog.title: Remove salts and keep the largest fragment

backlog.spec: Expand the training set by adding a copy of each training molecule with stereochemistry removed (Chem.RemoveStereochemistry) and a copy with a random SMILES enumeration (Chem.MolToSmiles with doRandom=True, seeded). Use the expanded set to train the RandomForest and predict on the unmodified test SMILES. Augmentation can make the model robust to representation noise.
backlog.title: Train-time augmentation with stereo-stripped SMILES

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train five RandomForest models with different random_state values derived from seed (seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4), each with 200 trees, and average their predict_proba outputs. Seed averaging reduces the variance of the final ranking at a modest compute cost. Keep the Morgan featurizer.
backlog.title: Bagged models averaged over seeds

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM with bagging_fraction=0.7, bagging_freq=1, feature_fraction=0.2, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=20, 300 trees, and learning_rate 0.05 on Morgan bits. Then wrap it with sklearn CalibratedClassifierCV(method='sigmoid', cv=3) using the training fold. Calibration makes the scores comparable across the ensemble members and can help when they are combined later.
backlog.title: Platt-calibrated gradient boosting with subsampling

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and the mean training label per scaffold, with a shrinkage prior toward the global positive rate (pseudo-count 5). Add these two features (scaffold target mean and count) to the Morgan bits and fit the RandomForest. For test molecules, use the scaffold mean if the scaffold was seen in training, otherwise the global rate. This uses the scaffold-level signal directly.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware target smoothing

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the binary:logistic XGBClassifier in the three-feature-set loop with XGBRanker (objective='rank:pairwise', one query group containing all training rows, lambdarank_pair_method='topk' or default, n_estimators=500, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Fit with qid = np.zeros(len(y)) and predict with model.predict(x_te) as the score instead of predict_proba. Keep the existing rank averaging across the three feature sets. The metric is AUROC, so a pairwise objective that directly orders positives above negatives may help.
backlog.title: Pairwise ranking objective for XGBoost

backlog.spec: Keep the three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble, but pass monotone_constraints to each XGBClassifier for the curated-descriptor feature set only, using prior BBB knowledge: TPSA decreasing (-1), H-bond donors decreasing (-1), H-bond acceptors decreasing (-1), acid count decreasing (-1), basic amine count neutral (0), and MW, logP, rotatable bonds and fraction sp3 unconstrained (0). Apply this to the descriptor set only, which is the 10-column matrix from featurize. Fingerprint sets stay unconstrained. The constraints add a physically motivated regularizer that should reduce overfitting to skeleton-specific patterns.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on physicochemical features

backlog.spec: Keep the three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble, but for each model average predictions taken at several boosting stages instead of only the final one. Train once with n_estimators=500, then compute predict_proba with iteration_range=(0, k) for k in {100, 200, 300, 400, 500} and average the resulting probabilities (or ranks) across those stages before the cross-feature-set rank averaging. This adds a cheap schedule-style ensemble over the training trajectory and needs no extra fits.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging across boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training data once with a stratified 15% holdout using the seed. For each of the three feature sets, fit XGBClassifier with learning_rate=0.02 and n_estimators=2000, early_stopping_rounds=100, and eval_metric='auc' on the holdout. Record best_iteration, then refit on the full training data with n_estimators set to the best iteration times 1.1 and predict the test molecules. Keep the rank averaging across feature sets. This replaces the fixed 500-round schedule with a data-driven one.
backlog.title: Inner-holdout early stopping for the boosting round count

backlog.spec: Transductive step inside fit_predict. First run the existing three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble on the training data and predict the test molecules. Take the test molecules whose averaged normalized score is in the top 15% as pseudo-positive and the bottom 15% as pseudo-negative, and append them with their pseudo-labels to the training set. Refit the same ensemble on the augmented set and return its rank-averaged predictions for the test molecules. Use the seed for everything. Only the test SMILES that the harness already passes in are used, so no outside data is involved.
backlog.title: Self-training with confident test-set pseudo-labels

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, for each feature set build 8 bags. Each bag keeps every minority-class training row and an equal-size random sample of majority-class rows, drawn with a seed-derived RandomState. Fit an XGBClassifier with the existing hyperparameters on each bag, use n_estimators=300 to keep runtime in budget, and accumulate rank-normalized test predictions. Average the bags within a feature set, then average across the three feature sets as before. Undersampling decorrelates the trees and can make the averaged score more robust to the class imbalance in the BBB labels.
backlog.title: Balanced undersampled bagging of the ensemble

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before the final fits, run a small random search over XGBoost settings on the training data only. Draw 6 configurations from max_depth in {3,4,5,6}, learning_rate in {0.02,0.05,0.1}, colsample_bytree in {0.2,0.3,0.5}, min_child_weight in {1,2,5}, and reg_lambda in {1,5}, with n_estimators chosen so that depth and learning rate give a similar total fit. Score each configuration with a stratified 3-fold inner AUROC on the training rows, using the seed for the splits and draws. Use the best configuration to refit the three feature-set models and predict the test molecules. Keep the rank averaging. Watch the 10-minute job cap: limit the search to the descriptor set and reuse the chosen configuration for the fingerprint sets if runtime is tight.
backlog.title: Per-fit random hyperparameter search with inner CV

backlog.spec: Keep the three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble, but change the regularization. Use max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators=1000, reg_lambda=5, reg_alpha=0.5, gamma=0.5, min_child_weight=5, subsample=0.7, and colsample_bytree=0.2, with random_state=seed and n_jobs=8. The shallower trees with a per-split loss penalty and stronger L1 and L2 terms should generalize better across unseen Murcko scaffolds than the current depth-5 setting. Everything else, including rank averaging, stays the same.
backlog.title: Strongly regularized shallow boosting

backlog.spec: Extend featurize with a few extra columns that approximate the charge state at pH 7.4, which drives BBB permeation. Add counts of quaternary or permanently charged nitrogen, amidine or guanidine groups (basic), tetrazole and acyl-sulfonamide groups (acidic), zwitterion flag (acid count and basic amine count both at least 1), halogen count (F, Cl, Br, I), and counts of N and O atoms. Build these with SMARTS patterns compiled once at module level. Concatenate them to the existing 10 columns to form the descriptor set. The fingerprint sets and the XGBoost settings are unchanged.
backlog.title: Ionization-state and heteroatom features for the descriptor set

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, for each feature set, create an augmented training set by mixing random pairs of training rows. Draw 0.5 times the training size of pairs with a Beta(0.4, 0.4) mixing weight, using a seed-derived RandomState. Mixed rows take the mixed features and the label of the row with the larger weight. Concatenate the mixed rows with the original rows and fit the existing XGBClassifier on the combined set. Predict the test molecules as before and keep the rank averaging. This smooths decision boundaries between neighboring fingerprint regions, which may help generalization to new skeletons.
backlog.title: Feature-level mixup augmentation before boosting

backlog.spec: Replace the XGBoost ensemble members with a Laplacian-corrected Bernoulli naive Bayes, the classic BBB baseline. Use the presence bits of the 2048-bit Morgan radius-2 fingerprint. For each bit b and class c, estimate P(bit on | c) as (n_bc + 1)/(n_c + 2), where n_bc counts training molecules of class c with bit b on. Score a test molecule by summing log-odds contributions over its on-bits and off-bits (both directions, with the same smoothing). Return the sigmoid of the summed log-odds as the probability of class 1. Add this as one extra member, and rank-average it with the existing XGBoost ensemble output. Use numpy only; there is no fitting loop, so it runs in well under a second.
backlog.title: Laplacian-corrected naive Bayes on Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Add a fourth feature set built from RDKit's pharmacophore-style reduced-graph fingerprint, rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint(mol), which is a fixed-length real vector. Train one XGBoost model on it with the same hyperparameters as the other members, and add its rank to the existing rank-sum. Do not change the other three feature sets. This tests whether a coarse pharmacophore view adds information the bit fingerprints miss.
backlog.title: Extended reduced-graph (ErG) fingerprint member

backlog.spec: Add a small block of 3D shape descriptors. For each molecule, add hydrogens, embed one conformer with rdDistGeom.ETKDGv3 using randomSeed=seed (fall back to 2D-only zeros if embedding fails), then MMFF-optimize it if possible. Compute the principal moments of inertia ratios (NPR1, NPR2), asphericity, eccentricity, radius of gyration, and the 3D polar surface area from rdMolDescriptors. Concatenate these with the existing curated 10-feature set and fit one XGBoost member on that combined vector. Keep all other members unchanged. Cap per-molecule embedding time with maxAttempts so the 15-fit job stays under 10 minutes.
backlog.title: 3D shape descriptors from a seeded conformer

backlog.spec: Before fitting each XGBoost member, compute the Murcko scaffold (generic or canonical, from rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold) for each training molecule. Give each molecule a sample weight of 1/sqrt(count of its scaffold in the training set), then rescale weights to mean 1. This stops large scaffold families from dominating the trees, which matters because the harness tests on unseen scaffolds. Pass the weights through the sample_weight argument of model.fit. Keep the rest of the ensemble unchanged.
backlog.title: Scaffold-frequency sample weighting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train a small logistic-regression or shallow XGBoost domain classifier to separate the training fingerprints (label 0) from the test fingerprints (label 1), using the Morgan bits. Convert its predicted probabilities p into importance weights p/(1-p), clipped to [0.1, 10] and normalized to mean 1. Use these weights as sample_weight when fitting each existing XGBoost member. The model is then tuned toward the test-set chemistry without using test labels. Keep the code to one helper function.
backlog.title: Covariate-shift importance weighting from a domain classifier

backlog.spec: Replace the single fit per feature set with bagged fits. For each of 8 bags (seeded by seed+bag index), draw training molecules by bootstrapping unique Murcko scaffolds with replacement, then taking all molecules that carry each drawn scaffold. Fit one XGBoost model per feature set on each bag. Average rank-scores across all bags and feature sets. This keeps the bootstrap at the scaffold level, which mirrors the harness split and reduces variance from scaffold-family composition. Reduce n_estimators to about 250 per bag to keep runtime within budget.
backlog.title: Scaffold-level bootstrap bagging

backlog.spec: Swap each XGBoost member's booster for DART by passing booster='dart' with rate_drop=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, and one_drop=True. Keep n_estimators near 300 and learning_rate near 0.1, because DART is slower per tree. Predict with the default ntree_limit behaviour. Use only the fingerprint/curated feature sets already in the ensemble. This is a regularization change, as tree dropout is a different regularizer from subsampling and depth limits.
backlog.title: DART booster with dropout over trees

backlog.spec: Replace the default logloss objective in each XGBoost member with a custom focal-loss objective, passed as obj= to XGBClassifier.fit or booster training. Use gamma=1.5 and alpha=0.5. Implement the gradient and hessian in numpy from the sigmoid of the raw margin: p=sigmoid(margin), pt=p for positives and 1-p for negatives, and derive the focal-loss grad/hess (floor the hessian at 1e-6). Use the probability sigmoid(margin) for prediction. Only the training loss changes; the feature sets and tree settings stay the same. This pushes the model toward hard, borderline molecules, which often decide AUROC.
backlog.title: Focal-loss custom objective for XGBoost

backlog.spec: Train each XGBoost member for 600 rounds at learning_rate 0.1 and use a cosine decay of the learning rate to 0.005 over the rounds, by calling xgb.train with a learning_rate callback, or equivalently with xgboost.callback.LearningRateScheduler. Save the test predictions at rounds 300, 450, and 600 using iteration_range, then average those three snapshot predictions in rank space. This is a schedule change that also gives a cheap ensemble from a single fit.
backlog.title: Learning-rate cosine schedule with snapshot averaging

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 3-fold stratified split on the training data, grouped by Murcko scaffold (use GroupKFold). Fit each feature-set XGBoost member on the inner training parts and compute out-of-fold predictions for every training molecule. Search a coarse grid of blend weights (for example 0, 0.5, 1, 2 for each member) and keep the weights that maximize inner out-of-fold AUROC from sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score. Then refit each member on all training data and use those weights for the test-set rank blend. This turns the equal-weight blend into a data-chosen blend, with a small cost in runtime.
backlog.title: Rank-averaging weights chosen by inner out-of-fold AUROC

backlog.spec: Add a new ensemble member that does not use boosting. Build a dense feature matrix from the 10 curated descriptors plus the 68 Wildman-Crippen atom-type counts (rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs, summed per type). Fit sklearn QuantileTransformer on the training fold only, then fit ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Rank-average its test probabilities with the existing XGBoost members, using equal weight per member.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees member on quantile-scaled descriptors and Crippen atom-type counts

backlog.spec: Keep the existing three XGBoost members unchanged. Add one more XGBoost member trained on a 68-column matrix of Wildman-Crippen atom-type counts, computed per molecule with rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs (count atoms by their Crippen type index). Use the same XGBoost hyperparameters as the other members. Average the four members by rank as before. This tests whether a compact, chemistry-typed count vector carries signal that Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS miss.
backlog.title: Crippen atom-type count feature set as a fourth XGBoost member

backlog.spec: Replace the atom-pair member with a low-dimensional latent model. Stack atom-pair count fingerprints (fpSize 2048) for all training and test molecules, apply log1p, then fit TruncatedSVD(n_components=128, random_state=seed) on the training fold only. Standardize the projected features and fit LogisticRegression(C=0.5, max_iter=2000). Use its probabilities as one member in the rank average with the Morgan and MACCS XGBoost members. The embedding turns sparse counts into dense, smooth coordinates for a model family that has not been tried on this feature set.
backlog.title: Latent semantic embedding of atom-pair counts with a linear classifier

backlog.spec: Build a graph over training and test molecules together. Use Morgan bit vectors and connect each node to its k=10 nearest neighbours by Tanimoto similarity, with edge weights equal to similarity raised to the power 3. Initialize training nodes with their labels (0 or 1) and test nodes with 0.5. Iterate label spreading, F <- alpha * S F + (1 - alpha) * Y0, with alpha=0.9 for 50 steps, clamping training nodes to their labels at each step. Output the converged test-node scores, rank-averaged with the XGBoost ensemble. This is a graph-based semi-supervised method, distinct from the earlier self-training attempt.
backlog.title: Label spreading over a Tanimoto kNN graph (transductive)

backlog.spec: Replace the final rank averaging with a calibrated log-probability product. For each ensemble member, fit a one-dimensional Platt scaler (LogisticRegression on its logit) using an inner stratified 5-fold out-of-fold prediction on the training fold only. Then, for each test molecule, sum the calibrated log-odds over members and pass the sum through a sigmoid to get the final probability. Keep the same three XGBoost members and seeds. This uses calibrated confidence rather than rank position, so confident members can dominate when they are right.
backlog.title: Product-of-experts blending with per-member Platt calibration

backlog.spec: Keep the three XGBoost members and their hyperparameters. Replace the hard 0/1 training labels with smoothed soft targets y_s = 0.05 + 0.9 * y, so positives sit at 0.95 and negatives at 0.05. Train with the standard binary logistic objective by passing the smoothed targets through a sample-duplication trick: duplicate every training row, one copy with label 1 at weight 0.95 and one with label 0 at weight 0.95, each positive row receiving weight 1 - 0.05 for its label and 0.05 for the opposite label. Average the members by rank as before. The regularization discourages overconfident leaves on noisy activity labels.
backlog.title: Label smoothing on XGBoost targets

backlog.spec: Before fitting the classifier, learn auxiliary regressors from fingerprints. Compute RDKit MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, and number of H-bond donors and acceptors for all training and test molecules. Using an inner 5-fold split on the training fold, fit an XGBRegressor per auxiliary target from the Morgan bit matrix, and produce out-of-fold predictions for training rows and full-model predictions for test rows. Append these five predicted values to the Morgan feature set for the classifier. Keep everything else unchanged. This injects a learned, smooth summary of physicochemistry into a sparse fingerprint model.
backlog.title: Auxiliary physicochemical targets stacked as features

backlog.spec: For each of the three feature sets (Morgan, atom-pair, MACCS), fit three XGBoost models with max_depth 3, 5 and 7 instead of one depth-5 model. Keep learning_rate=0.05 and n_estimators=500 for depth 5, and scale n_estimators to 400 for depth 3 and 600 for depth 7 so training stays under the time limit. Rank-average all nine predictions with equal weight. This gives a bias-variance spread over tree complexity without changing the feature sets.
backlog.title: Mixture of XGBoost depths per feature set

backlog.spec: Add a fourth feature set built from RDKit's Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprint (rdReducedGraphs or Gobbi_Pharm2D.GetPharm2DFingerprint with the default factory). Convert the sparse result to a dense count vector of fixed length (or hash it to 2048 bits). Train one XGBoost member on it with the same hyperparameters, and add it to the rank average. The Gobbi fingerprint encodes donor, acceptor, aromatic, cation and anion pair distances, which is pharmacology-oriented and not a substructure-hash fingerprint.
backlog.title: Pharmacophore-pair (Gobbi) fingerprint member

backlog.spec: For each feature set, first fit the XGBoost model as now and compute out-of-fold predictions on the training fold with an inner stratified 5-fold split. Set each training molecule's sample weight to 1 plus 2 times its out-of-fold absolute error |p - y|. Refit the XGBoost model on the same features with these weights (sample_weight argument of fit) and use the refitted model for the test predictions. Rank-average the three refitted members as before. This focuses the second fit on molecules the first fit gets wrong, similar in spirit to boosting across models.
backlog.title: Hard-example reweighting in a second boosting pass

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, for each feature set, first fit a cheap XGBoost (150 rounds, depth 4) on the training fold and get out-of-fold predictions from a 4-fold split of the training molecules only. Keep the 75% of training molecules with the smallest OOF log-loss as stage-1 data, and train the depth-5, 500-round model on that subset. Then continue boosting from that model (xgb_model argument of fit) on the full training set for 200 more rounds at learning rate 0.02. Everything is seeded by the seed argument. The rest of the ensemble and rank averaging stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Curriculum two-stage XGBoost

backlog.spec: For each feature set in the ensemble, add 4 columns to the XGBoost input. They are the mean label of the 5 nearest training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on the Morgan bits, the max similarity to a positive training molecule, the max similarity to a negative training molecule, and their difference. For training rows, compute these columns out-of-fold: use a 5-fold split inside the training set, and for each row use only neighbours from the other folds. For test rows, use all training molecules. The neighbour features are appended to each member's existing fingerprint matrix. Use the seed argument for the inner split.
backlog.title: Stacked Tanimoto-neighbour label features

backlog.spec: Add a fourth XGBoost ensemble member trained on two new feature blocks. The first is RDKit EState fingerprint counts (rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol, 79 values) and the EState atom-type indices summed per molecule. The second is a hashed count vector of BRICS fragments (BRICS.BRICSDecompose on each molecule, hashed into 1024 buckets with a fixed hash function). Concatenate the two blocks for this member only. Keep the other three members unchanged and average the four members by rank as before.
backlog.title: EState and BRICS fragment-count member

backlog.spec: Add a fourth XGBoost member that uses only ring-topology features. For each molecule, take its ring systems (fused or spiro groups of rings), replace every atom with carbon and every bond with single to get the generic framework, and count the following: ring systems by hashed generic SMILES into 512 buckets, number of ring systems, number of aromatic rings, largest ring-system size, and number of ring atoms. Use the hashed counts as the feature matrix. Keep the other three members and the rank averaging unchanged.
backlog.title: Ring-system and generic-scaffold count member

backlog.spec: Replace the three per-feature-set XGBoost fits with a random-subspace ensemble. Stack the Morgan, atom-pair, MACCS and the 10 curated descriptors into one matrix. Train 24 XGBoost models, each on a random 25% of the columns sampled with the seed argument plus the model index, using 400 rounds, depth 5, learning rate 0.05 and subsample 0.8. Average the 24 models by rank. Use n_jobs=8 and keep total runtime under 10 minutes for the 15 fits.
backlog.title: Random-subspace XGBoost over pooled features

backlog.spec: Before fitting each XGBoost member, make 3 augmented copies of the training matrix. In each copy, randomly set 10% of the nonzero fingerprint entries to zero (not the curated descriptor columns), with the random generator seeded from seed and the copy index. Stack the original and the 3 copies and fit one XGBoost model on all 4x rows, with the same hyperparameters but 300 rounds. Predict on the unaltered test matrix. Keep the feature sets, rank averaging and everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Input bit-dropout augmentation

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest-free ensemble member on Morgan count fingerprints with a Gaussian-process binary classifier. Use the Tanimoto kernel K(a,b) = sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)) on the count Morgan vectors. Fit by Laplace approximation with a Newton iteration (about 20 steps, no sklearn GaussianProcessClassifier), with a kernel-scale hyperparameter chosen by the marginal likelihood on a grid of 5 values. Use the predicted latent mean passed through the sigmoid as the probability. Add it to the rank average as a fourth member with equal weight. Keep the XGBoost members unchanged.
backlog.title: Gaussian-process classifier with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Two-stage distillation inside fit_predict. First, train the existing three-member XGBoost ensemble on the training fold and get out-of-fold probabilities for the training molecules with a 4-fold split of the training set. Second, train a student XGBoost regressor (reg:squarederror, 400 rounds, depth 4, learning rate 0.05) on the same fingerprint and descriptor features, with the OOF teacher probabilities as continuous targets. Predict test molecules with the student and average its rank with the teacher's rank 50/50. Use the seed argument in all splits and models.
backlog.title: Soft distillation from an inner teacher ensemble

backlog.spec: For each feature-set XGBoost member, add conservative leaf control. Set gamma=1.0 (minimum split loss), reg_lambda=5, reg_alpha=0.5, and max_delta_step=1 to limit each leaf's update size. Keep depth 5, 500 rounds, learning rate 0.05, subsample 0.8 and colsample_bytree 0.3. Then train a second copy of each member with gamma=0 and the same other settings, and rank-average the two copies within each feature set before the cross-set rank averaging. Seed everything with the seed argument.
backlog.title: Penalised shrinkage of boosted leaves with gamma and max_delta_step

backlog.spec: Add a single extra XGBoost model trained only on the 10 curated descriptors (TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, Fsp3, formal charge, acid count, basic amine count). Use monotone_constraints that make the predicted probability decrease with TPSA, HBD, HBA, acid count and MolWt, and increase with MolLogP and Fsp3, with depth 3, 300 rounds and learning rate 0.05. Its rank is added to the existing three-member rank average with weight 1.5. Seed with the seed argument. This tests whether a physically constrained model generalises across scaffolds better than the flexible members.
backlog.title: Monotone-constrained gradient boosting on the curated descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a fourth XGBoost ensemble member in fingerprints(). Compute RDKit's Avalon count fingerprint (rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP, nBits=1024) and the RDKit topological (path-based) fingerprint (Chem.RDKFingerprint, fpSize=2048, maxPath=6) for every molecule, convert each to a float32 numpy array, and append them to the existing list of feature sets. The fit_predict loop already fits one XGBoost per feature set and rank-averages the test predictions, so the new member only needs to be added to the zip of train and test sets. Keep all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Avalon and RDKit topological fingerprint ensemble member

backlog.spec: Extend featurize() so that, in addition to the 10 curated columns, it appends all pairwise products of the continuous columns (TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, Fsp3) and the ratio TPSA/MolWt, giving roughly 30 columns. Standardise nothing, since trees are invariant to scale. Use this matrix as the descriptor feature set in the existing XGBoost ensemble (replace the current descriptor-only member, leave the Morgan and atom-pair members unchanged). Seeded XGBoost settings stay as they are.
backlog.title: Pairwise interaction features on the curated descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the final rank-average step by a stacked member. Fit an ExtraTreesClassifier (400 trees, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed) on the concatenated Morgan+MACCS bits. Use model.apply(X) to get the leaf index of every sample in every tree, one-hot encode those leaf indices with sklearn's OneHotEncoder (handle_unknown='ignore') fitted on training leaves, and train an L2 LogisticRegression (C=0.05, max_iter=2000) on the one-hot matrix. The test-side probability from this logistic regression is rank-averaged with the existing XGBoost ensemble members as one additional member. This is a random-forest kernel feature map followed by a linear model, distinct from the earlier single-model linear swap.
backlog.title: Leaf-embedding logistic regression on ExtraTrees

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before the real fit, run a 5-fold inner stratified CV on the training molecules only (StratifiedKFold with shuffle and random_state=seed) using the existing XGBoost ensemble on a fast setting (200 rounds). Compute the out-of-fold predicted probability for each training molecule and drop the 5 percent of training molecules whose out-of-fold probability is most confidently wrong (largest distance between predicted probability and their label). Then fit the full ensemble on the cleaned training set and predict the test set as before. The test molecules are never used for cleaning. This tests whether removing mislabelled or atypical training molecules improves ranking on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Label-noise cleaning before the final fit

backlog.spec: Split the training molecules into two regimes by MolWt, with a cutoff at 350 Da (the cutoff is a fixed constant, not tuned). Train two independent copies of the existing XGBoost-on-three-feature-sets ensemble, one on each regime, each seeded with seed. For a test molecule, use the expert of its own regime when it has at least 100 training molecules in that regime; otherwise fall back to a single model trained on all data. Combine the outputs by rank averaging over the full test set so that the final score is comparable across regimes. This is a gating-by-size mixture of experts that lets the boundary between penetrant and non-penetrant molecules differ between small and large molecules.
backlog.title: Molecular-weight regime mixture of experts

backlog.spec: Add a non-tree member that works on the curated descriptor matrix. Quantile-transform each column to a normal distribution with sklearn QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=200), fitted on the training fold only. Generate 1000 random Fourier features z(x) = sqrt(2/D) cos(W x + b) with W drawn from a Gaussian with scale gamma=0.1 and b uniform on [0, 2 pi), both drawn from numpy RandomState(seed). Fit a LogisticRegression (C=1.0, max_iter=2000) on z(x) and rank-average its test probabilities with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight. This approximates an RBF-kernel SVM on physicochemical descriptors, a smooth model that is structurally different from the tree members.
backlog.title: Random Fourier feature logistic model on descriptors

backlog.spec: Add one extra ensemble member that is a LightGBM booster rather than XGBoost. Use LGBMClassifier with extra_trees=True (randomised split thresholds), path_smooth=1.0, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=5, n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1, and random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, applied to the 2048-bit Morgan counts. Rank-average its test probabilities with the existing three XGBoost members at equal weight. Extra randomised thresholds plus path smoothing act as a strong regulariser, a different inductive bias from the depth-wise XGBoost members.
backlog.title: LightGBM with extra_trees and path smoothing on Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Replace the depth-based tree used on the curated descriptor matrix with an XGBoost model that has tree_method='hist', booster='gbtree', linear_tree=True (each leaf fits a linear model on the features used by its split), max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.05, n_estimators=300, reg_lambda=1.0, and random_state=seed. Keep the fingerprint feature sets unchanged. This makes the descriptor member able to model smooth, near-linear trends in TPSA, MolWt and logP within each region of descriptor space, which tree leaves approximate only with step functions.
backlog.title: XGBoost linear-tree booster on curated descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute a per-training-molecule sample weight that down-weights over-represented chemotypes. For the Morgan 2048-bit presence fingerprints of the training molecules, compute the pairwise Tanimoto similarity matrix (numpy, bitwise AND and OR counts). For each molecule, count neighbours with similarity at least 0.6 (including itself) and set its weight to 1/count, then rescale weights to have mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight in every XGBoost fit call in the ensemble. Unlike scaffold-level weighting, this operates on fingerprint similarity, so near-duplicate analogues from different scaffolds are also down-weighted, reducing the influence of dense analogue series on the learned decision boundary.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-density de-clustering weights

backlog.spec: For each XGBoost member, train with learning_rate=0.05 and n_estimators=500 as now, but instead of predicting with the final model, obtain test predictions at rounds 300, 350, 400, 450 and 500 using model.predict_proba(X, iteration_range=(0, r)) and average these probabilities over the five checkpoints before rank-averaging the members. This is a cheap form of weight averaging over the tail of boosting, which reduces variance from the final few rounds of overfitting on unseen scaffolds, and requires no extra training time.
backlog.title: Stochastic weight averaging over late boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Compute a CNS multiparameter-optimisation style score with no fitted parameters. For each molecule, take RDKit values for ClogP, MW, TPSA, HBD, most basic pKa proxy (count of BASIC_AMINE matches as a 0/1 proxy), and acid count. Map each to a desirability in [0,1] with fixed piecewise-linear ramps (e.g. TPSA full score below 60 and zero above 120, HBD full score at 0 to 1 and zero above 3, MW full score below 360 and zero above 500, ClogP full score in 1 to 3). Sum the six desirabilities into a score in [0,6]. Rank-transform this score on test molecules and add it to the existing rank-sum in fit_predict with weight 0.5 relative to each XGBoost member. No extra learning, and the seed is unused for this member.
backlog.title: Parameter-free CNS MPO desirability as a rank member

backlog.spec: Add a fourth feature set built from hashed Morgan count fingerprints at radius 1 with 1024 bits and at radius 3 with 4096 bits, both with includeChirality=False. Train one XGBoost member per set using the existing hyperparameters, and rank-average all members as now. This tests whether the radius-2 Morgan choice is limiting, without changing the other members. Keep the code path identical to the current Morgan generator, just parameterised by radius and size.
backlog.title: Multi-scale Morgan counts at radius 1 and 3

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, build a binary matrix of Morgan radius-2 presence bits for the training molecules. For each bit, compute the smoothed positive rate across training molecules that carry it, with smoothing toward the global prior using m=10 pseudo-counts. Compute these rates out-of-fold with a 5-fold split of the training set (stratified, seeded) so that a training molecule never encodes itself. For each molecule, average the encoded rates over its set bits, and also take min and max, giving a 3-feature summary. Feed these 3 features plus the 10 curated descriptors into a single XGBoost model. Test molecules use rates fitted on the full training set.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold substructure target encoding

backlog.spec: Replace the XGBoost members with a rotation forest of 200 trees. For each tree, randomly partition the standardised feature space (curated descriptors plus 2048-bit Morgan bits selected to the 300 most frequent in training) into subsets of 10 features. For each subset fit PCA on a seeded 75% bootstrap of the training rows, and stack the rotated components to form the tree's input. Fit a sklearn DecisionTreeClassifier with max_depth=None and min_samples_leaf=2 on the rotated data. Average predicted probabilities across trees. Use the seed for all partitions and bootstraps. This gives oblique splits that tree ensembles on raw bits cannot form.
backlog.title: Rotation-forest style oblique trees on descriptors plus fingerprints

backlog.spec: Build the matrix of Morgan radius-2 bits plus MACCS keys for both training and test molecules together (unsupervised, so test features are allowed). Train a sklearn MLPRegressor with a single hidden layer of 256 ReLU units and a 32-unit bottleneck, which is an autoencoder over this matrix (use two MLPRegressor stages or a manual numpy autoencoder), fit with max_iter=200 and random_state=seed. Take the 32-unit bottleneck activations as dense features and concatenate them with the curated descriptors. Train one XGBoost model on this feature set and rank-average it with the existing members. Labels are never used in the autoencoder.
backlog.title: Transductive autoencoder bottleneck features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, get out-of-fold predicted probabilities for the training molecules from the existing XGBoost ensemble using a 5-fold split of the training set. Compute residuals r = y - p_oof. For each test molecule, find its k=10 nearest training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on Morgan radius-2 bits and compute a similarity-weighted mean residual (weights = similarity to the power 3). Add this correction, scaled by 0.5, to the ensemble's probability on the test molecule before the final rank step. Clip to [0,1] before ranking. Training molecules' own residuals must never be used for their own correction, which the out-of-fold step guarantees.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-neighbour residual correction

backlog.spec: Keep the current three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble structure, but build each feature set at three hashing widths: Morgan and atom-pair at 512, 1024 and 4096 bits, and MACCS unchanged. Train one XGBoost model per (feature set, width) pair, so 6 members in total, each with the existing hyperparameters and seed. Rank-average all members with equal weight. The aim is to diversify collision patterns across members rather than to add a new chemical view. Keep the total runtime in budget by reducing n_estimators to 350 for the 4096-bit members.
backlog.title: Hashed-size diversity ensemble

backlog.spec: Add a member that fits a discrete AdaBoost (SAMME with two classes) ensemble of 300 depth-2 DecisionTreeClassifier stumps via sklearn AdaBoostClassifier with learning_rate=0.1 and random_state=seed. Use as input the concatenation of the curated descriptors and the 300 Morgan bits most frequent in training. Rank-average its predict_proba output with the XGBoost members at equal weight. This is a different boosting loss (exponential, reweighting hard examples) from the logistic loss used by XGBoost, so it gives a diverse member at low cost.
backlog.title: SAMME discrete AdaBoost on depth-2 trees

backlog.spec: Fit a fast XGBoost model (depth 3, 100 rounds, learning rate 0.1) on the 10 curated descriptors alone, using 5-fold out-of-fold predictions on the training set to produce per-molecule logit margins. Use these out-of-fold logits as base_margin when training the existing fingerprint XGBoost members, so each fingerprint model boosts from the descriptor prior rather than from zero. For test molecules, use the descriptor model fitted on all training data as base_margin. The final output is still the rank-average of the members. This turns the descriptor model into a warm start for the fingerprint boosters instead of a stacked feature.
backlog.title: Descriptor-prior margin for fingerprint boosting

backlog.spec: Run the entire three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble across 3 inner seeds derived from the seed argument (seed, seed+1000, seed+2000). In each inner run, apply a random permutation of columns in the 2048-bit Morgan matrix only for the training and test matrices together, which changes which bits share tree splits without changing information. Average the rank-normalised outputs over the 3 inner runs before returning. Keep n_estimators at 500 and reduce n_jobs contention by fitting the inner runs sequentially. Target runtime is under 3 minutes per job, well inside the 10-minute limit.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged bagging of the full ensemble with feature-column shuffle

backlog.spec: Inside featurize-style code, build a Burden-type matrix per molecule: diagonal entries are atomic properties (Gasteiger charge, Crippen logP contribution, atomic mass scaled, polarizability proxy), off-diagonal entries are 1 for bonded atoms and 0 otherwise. Take the largest 8 and smallest 8 eigenvalues of that matrix as 16 features, with 0 for empty molecules. Train one XGBoost (same settings as the incumbent members) on these BCUT features concatenated with the 10 curated descriptors, and rank-average its test probabilities with the existing three members. Use the seed for XGBoost random_state.
backlog.title: BCUT eigenvalue descriptors as a fourth XGBoost member

backlog.spec: Replace the fingerprint members with a small graph network written in numpy only. Atoms get a one-hot vector (element, degree, aromaticity, formal charge, H count) and bonds get a type vector. Run 3 rounds of message passing: each atom sums transformed neighbour states weighted by a learned bond-type matrix, then applies a ReLU update with hidden size 64. Pool by sum and mean over atoms, then a logistic output. Train with full-batch Adam (lr 0.01, weight decay 1e-4, 300 epochs) on the training molecules, using the seed for weight init. Hand-write the backward pass or use a finite-difference-free manual gradient; keep the total fit time under 60 seconds per fold. Rank-average its test probabilities with the incumbent ensemble.
backlog.title: Pure-numpy message-passing graph neural network

backlog.spec: Build a generalized additive logistic model. For each of the 10 curated descriptors, expand the value into a cubic B-spline basis with 6 knots placed at training-set quantiles, giving about 60 columns. Fit an L2-penalized logistic regression (C around 0.5, lbfgs, max_iter 2000) on the standardized spline columns from the training set only. Add this as a fourth rank-averaged member next to the incumbent XGBoost ensemble. Use scipy.interpolate.BSpline or sklearn SplineTransformer for the basis, and the seed only if a tie-breaking shuffle is needed.
backlog.title: Spline-basis additive logistic model on curated descriptors

backlog.spec: In each XGBoost member of the three-feature-set ensemble, set scale_pos_weight to (number of negatives / number of positives) computed from the training labels of that fit. Keep every other hyperparameter as in the incumbent. This reweights the logloss so that the minority class gets equal total gradient mass, which can change the ranking of borderline molecules even though AUROC is threshold-free. Compute the ratio inside fit_predict so it adapts to each fold.
backlog.title: Class-balanced XGBoost with scale_pos_weight

backlog.spec: Change the XGBoost members to grow_policy='lossguide' with max_leaves=31 and max_depth=0, keeping learning_rate 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 2 and 500 rounds. Lossguide expands the leaf with the largest loss reduction first, so the tree budget is spent where the signal is instead of on uniform depth. Apply this to all three feature sets and rank-average as before. Pass random_state=seed.
backlog.title: Lossguide growth with a leaf budget

backlog.spec: Replace the constant subsample=0.8 in each XGBoost member with a schedule that starts at 0.5 and rises linearly to 0.95 over the 500 rounds. Implement this by training in 10 consecutive chunks of 50 rounds: for each chunk, set subsample to the chunk value and continue training from the previous booster using xgb_model. Keep the same learning rate and tree settings. The aim is to explore broadly early and fit tightly late, without any validation data.
backlog.title: Annealed row-subsampling schedule across boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Before fitting, cluster the training molecules with Butina clustering on Morgan Tanimoto distances at a 0.6 threshold. Build 12 bags: each bag drops a random 25% of clusters (drawn with the seed) and trains one XGBoost per feature set on the remaining molecules. Average the rank-normalized test predictions over all bags and feature sets. The point is to make each member see a different chemotype mix, which should help generalization to unseen scaffolds. Keep the per-bag XGBoost size small (300 rounds) so the job stays under the 10-minute limit.
backlog.title: Butina-cluster hold-out bagging

backlog.spec: Create 3 augmented copies of the training matrix for each XGBoost member. In each copy, zero out (set to 0) all columns of one randomly chosen group among the Morgan bits, atom-pair counts and MACCS keys for a random 15% of rows, so the model learns to rely on several representations rather than one. Stack the original and the augmented rows (4 times the training size) with the original labels, train the usual XGBoost with the same settings, and predict on unmasked test features. Use np.random.default_rng(seed) for the masks.
backlog.title: Feature-group masking during boosting

backlog.spec: After the ensemble produces its rank-normalized test score, compute for each test molecule the mean training label of training molecules that share its Murcko generic scaffold (ring skeleton with atom types removed), falling back to the global positive rate if there are none. Blend the ensemble score with this prior using p_final = (1 - w) * p_ens + w * p_scaffold, with w = 0.2 and p_ens rescaled to [0,1]. This tests whether the label is shared within a skeleton family despite the scaffold-disjoint folds, using only training labels and no test labels.
backlog.title: Scaffold-family shrinkage of predictions

backlog.spec: Concatenate the 2048 Morgan presence bits and the 167 MACCS bits for each molecule, then fit sklearn LinearSVC (C=0.05, loss='squared_hinge', max_iter 5000, class_weight='balanced', random_state=seed). Convert decision values to probabilities with a Platt sigmoid fitted on the training decision values using a 5-fold inner cross-validation (CalibratedClassifierCV with method='sigmoid'). Add this as a fourth rank-averaged member. A linear max-margin model is a different inductive bias from the tree members and is cheap to fit.
backlog.title: Linear SVM with Platt scaling on concatenated Morgan and MACCS bits

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, quantile-scale the 10 curated descriptors using training-set quantiles (fit on train only, then apply to test). For each test molecule, compute a Gaussian-kernel Parzen estimate of the positive-class density and of the negative-class density over the training molecules, with bandwidth set by Scott's rule on the scaled features. Score = log(p_pos) - log(p_neg) with a small additive epsilon, and return the rank-normalised score in [0, 1]. Use it as one rank-averaged member next to the existing XGBoost ensemble, with weight 1. No randomness is involved, so seed is unused.
backlog.title: Parzen density-ratio classifier on curated descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace one fingerprint member with a sequential-covering rule learner. Build candidate single-feature threshold conditions from quantile cut points (10 per descriptor) on the 10 curated descriptors. Greedily grow up to 15 conjunctive rules of length at most 3: each rule is chosen to maximise the Laplace-smoothed precision of positives on the still-uncovered training molecules, then removes the molecules it covers. The score for a molecule is the Laplace-smoothed positive rate of the first rule it matches, or the base rate if none match. Return the normalised score. Use seed only for tie-breaking shuffles. Add it as one rank-averaged member.
backlog.title: Greedy rule-set learner on curated descriptor thresholds

backlog.spec: Extend featurize with an estimated distribution-coefficient feature. Count carboxylic acids (existing ACID pattern), basic aliphatic amines (existing BASIC_AMINE pattern), and quaternary or permanently charged nitrogens. Estimate an approximate pKa per group (acid about 4.5, aliphatic amine about 9.5) and compute logD7.4 ~= MolLogP - log10(1 + 10**(7.4 - pKa_acid)*n_acid) - log10(1 + 10**(pKa_base - 7.4)*n_base), clipped to [-5, 8]. Append this logD value and the count of ionised groups to the curated descriptor matrix that feeds the existing ensemble member. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Ionization-corrected logD estimate as a feature

backlog.spec: Define a fixed list of about 60 SMARTS patterns for groups relevant to BBB penetration: amides, sulfonamides, sulfonyl groups, phenols, anilines, nitro groups, aryl halides, esters, ethers, ureas, carbamates, nitriles, hydroxyl groups, quaternary ammonium, tertiary amines, pyridines, imidazoles, and so on. For each molecule, count matches of each pattern with GetSubstructMatches and build a 60-column integer matrix. Train one XGBoost model (same hyperparameters as the existing members) on this matrix, and add its rank to the ensemble sum. Keep the other three members unchanged.
backlog.title: Functional-group SMARTS count library as a fourth member

backlog.spec: For the curated descriptor member only, augment the training set with 4 noisy copies of each training molecule. Each copy adds independent Gaussian noise to every descriptor, with standard deviation equal to 0.05 times that descriptor's training-set standard deviation, and keeps the original label. Fit one XGBoost model on the stacked 5x data (same hyperparameters, with min_child_weight scaled to 5) using seed-derived noise. Predict on unperturbed test descriptors and add the rank to the ensemble sum. This is a regularisation through input noise rather than tree-structure changes.
backlog.title: Gaussian jitter augmentation on curated descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a fourth member: a logistic regression trained with AdaGrad-style minibatch SGD on 2048-bit hashed Morgan count features, log1p-transformed and standardised using training statistics. Use L2 penalty 1e-4, batch size 64, 30 epochs, and a learning rate of 0.1 decayed as 0.1/sqrt(epoch+1). Shuffle each epoch with a RandomState seeded by the seed argument. Return the average of the weight vectors over the last 10 epochs (Polyak averaging) and use that averaged model for predictions. Rank-normalise its test probabilities and add them to the ensemble sum with weight 1.
backlog.title: Polyak-averaged minibatch logistic regression on Morgan counts

backlog.spec: For each of the three existing XGBoost members, draw a bootstrap sample of the training molecules with the seed. Train with a large budget of 1500 rounds using learning rate 0.05 and record the log-loss on the out-of-bag molecules at every round via evals_result. Choose the round count that minimises out-of-bag log-loss, clipped to [150, 800]. Refit a model on the full training set with that round count (not on the bootstrap sample) and use it for prediction. This replaces the fixed 500-round setting for these members and keeps the rest of the ensemble unchanged.
backlog.title: Out-of-bag early stopping per boosting member

backlog.spec: Instead of the usual row subsampling, give each of the three existing XGBoost members a Bayesian bootstrap: draw non-negative weights from a Dirichlet(1,...,1) distribution over the training molecules (scaled so the weights average 1), with a separate draw per member, using a RandomState seeded from the seed argument. Pass them as sample_weight to fit. Set the model's subsample parameter to 1.0 so the weights are the only source of randomness. Keep all hyperparameters otherwise unchanged and rank-average the three members as before.
backlog.title: Dirichlet bootstrap sample weights per ensemble member

backlog.spec: After computing the ensemble's normalised score for every test molecule, smooth it over the test set itself. Compute Tanimoto similarity between the Morgan bit vectors of all test molecules. For each test molecule, take its k=5 most similar other test molecules (similarity above 0.3, otherwise ignore) and replace its score with a 0.7/0.3 blend of its own score and the similarity-weighted mean of its neighbours' scores. Use only the test-set scores and fingerprints, so no labels are involved and the procedure is consistent across folds. Return the smoothed scores rank-normalised to [0, 1].
backlog.title: Transductive kNN smoothing of test scores

backlog.spec: Add a fourth member: an SVC with an RBF kernel (probability=False) on the 10 curated descriptors after quantile transformation to a normal distribution, with statistics fitted on the training molecules only. Set C=1.0 and gamma='scale', and class_weight='balanced'. Use decision_function on the test molecules as the score, rank-normalise it, and add it to the rank-average ensemble with weight 1. The SVM is deterministic, so seed is unused here. This tests a kernel model on descriptors that is different from the earlier Tanimoto SVM and the tree models.
backlog.title: RBF-kernel SVM on quantile-scaled curated descriptors

backlog.spec: Append a small block of composition features to the curated descriptor matrix in featurize(): counts of N, O, S, F, Cl, Br, I and P atoms, fraction of aromatic heavy atoms, and count of halogens. Compute them from the RDKit mol with simple atom loops. Keep the descriptor block as a separate feature set so it becomes one more XGBoost member in the existing rank-averaged ensemble, with the same XGBoost settings. Do not change the fingerprints or the existing members.
backlog.title: Element-composition and aromaticity count features

backlog.spec: Build a fixed-length feature vector that counts pairs of hydrogen-bond donor atoms and acceptor atoms (use Lipinski-style SMARTS for donors and acceptors) binned by topological shortest-path distance, with bins 1 to 10 and a final overflow bin. Use Chem.GetDistanceMatrix. Treat it as a new feature set and fit one XGBoost member on it inside the existing ensemble loop. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Donor-acceptor topological-distance histogram

backlog.spec: Before the XGBoost members are fit, fit an L1-penalised LogisticRegression (solver liblinear) on the concatenated Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS bits, scaled to unit variance. Choose C by a stratified 3-fold inner CV on AUROC over a small grid (0.01, 0.03, 0.1). Keep only the columns with nonzero coefficients (cap at the 400 largest by absolute coefficient) and feed that reduced matrix to each XGBoost member. Use the seed for any shuffling.
backlog.title: L1-logistic gate for feature selection before boosting

backlog.spec: Use XGBoost's custom-objective hook, or a short numpy loop around a custom booster, to add decaying Gaussian noise to each new tree's leaf values during training (stochastic gradient Langevin-style). Noise standard deviation starts at 0.05 times the mean leaf magnitude and decays linearly to zero over the boosting rounds. Keep the same number of rounds, depth and learning rate as the incumbent XGBoost members, and seed the noise generator from the seed argument.
backlog.title: Noisy-leaf boosting with decaying Gaussian perturbation

backlog.spec: Precompute a pool of 6 to 8 cheap members (the existing three XGBoost feature sets plus ExtraTrees on Morgan bits and a logistic regression on descriptors). Score each member's predictions with a stratified 3-fold inner CV on the training data, and run greedy forward selection with replacement (up to 8 steps) on rank-averaged AUROC. Average only the selected members' ranks for the test predictions. Keep the outer fit_predict signature unchanged.
backlog.title: Greedy forward selection over a pool of precomputed members

backlog.spec: For each XGBoost member, train once for 1000 rounds on a 80/20 stratified split of the training data, and record the holdout log-loss or AUROC at every 50 rounds. Pick the round count that maximises the holdout AUROC, smoothed by a 3-point moving average, and then refit the member on the full training data with that round count. Use the seed argument for the split. Keep depth, learning rate and colsample settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Per-member round count from one learning-curve pass

backlog.spec: Replace each single XGBoost fit with two phases. Phase one trains 200 rounds at max_depth 6 with learning rate 0.1 using xgb_model from the booster. Phase two continues training on the same booster for 300 rounds at max_depth 3 with learning rate 0.05, reusing the first booster via xgb_model. Predict with the final booster. Apply this to each feature set in the ensemble and keep the rank averaging as it is.
backlog.title: Two-phase boosting with depth switch by continuation

backlog.spec: Before training, generate derived molecules from each training molecule with two RDKit reaction SMARTS edits: remove a terminal methyl group, and add a hydroxyl to an aromatic carbon with an open valence. Keep the original label for every derived molecule that parses and sanitises, and skip the rest. Concatenate the derived molecules to the training set only (not the test set), fit the existing ensemble on the augmented set, and predict the original test molecules. Use a fixed cap of 2 derived molecules per training molecule.
backlog.title: Counterfactual matched-pair augmentation with reaction SMARTS

backlog.spec: After computing the rank-averaged test scores, group the test molecules by Murcko generic scaffold. Replace each test score with a blend of 0.5 times its own score and 0.5 times the mean score of its scaffold group, provided the group has at least 2 members. Leave singleton groups unchanged. Check the blend weight on the training data with the same procedure inside an inner scaffold-grouped split before using it on the test set.
backlog.title: Scaffold-group test score averaging with an inner-fold blend

backlog.spec: For the Morgan bits, replace the raw presence features with an empirical-Bayes class-conditional rate per bit. For each bit, estimate the positive-class rate with a beta prior centred on the global rate, using a prior strength of 10 pseudo-counts, computed only from the training fold. Append these log-odds-ratio encodings as a separate feature set for one XGBoost member. Compute the encodings inside fit_predict so no test labels leak into them.
backlog.title: Beta-binomial empirical-Bayes bit encoding

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, stack the Morgan count fingerprints of train and test molecules into one matrix, fit sklearn TruncatedSVD (or PCA on the log1p counts) with 64 components using random_state=seed, and append the 64 projected coordinates to the curated 10-descriptor matrix. Fit one XGBClassifier (the existing depth-5 settings) on that combined matrix and return its rank-normalised test probabilities. The projection is unsupervised, so it uses test SMILES only as inputs, never their labels. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Transductive PCA embedding of count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Extend featurize with a few integer and ratio features: the number of Lipinski violations (MW>500, cLogP>5, HBD>5, HBA>10), the number of Veber violations (rotatable bonds>10, TPSA>140), the number of Ghose violations (MW outside 160-480, cLogP outside -0.4 to 5.6, heavy atoms outside 20-70, molar refractivity outside 40-130), and the ratios TPSA/MW, HBD/HBA and cLogP/TPSA (use 0 when the denominator is 0). Keep the existing XGBoost model and feature sets; only the curated descriptor matrix changes.
backlog.title: Drug-likeness rule-violation counts and property ratios

backlog.spec: Compute Gasteiger partial charges with rdkit.Chem.rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges on each molecule and derive: the most positive and most negative atomic partial charge, the sum of absolute charges over polar heavy atoms (N and O), the count of atoms with |charge|>0.2, and the mean charge over heavy atoms. Replace any NaN with 0. Append these five values to the curated descriptor matrix and keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Charge distribution is a physically motivated proxy for membrane permeation that TPSA and HBD/HBA do not capture.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge surface descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a new member that works directly on the raw SMILES text. Use sklearn TfidfVectorizer with analyzer='char', ngram_range=(2,6), min_df=2, sublinear_tf=True, and fit it on train_smiles only. Train LogisticRegression(C=2.0, max_iter=3000, class_weight=None, random_state=seed) on the sparse matrix, predict test probabilities, and rank-average them with the existing XGBoost members (equal weight, then normalise to [0,1]). The text model is trained on a different representation from the fingerprints, so its errors should be partly uncorrelated with theirs.
backlog.title: Character n-gram TF-IDF logistic model on SMILES strings

backlog.spec: Replace one ensemble member with a multiple-instance learner. For each molecule, every heavy atom is an instance described by a vector of its element, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, H count, ring membership and a Morgan radius-1 environment hashed to 256 bits. Train a logistic regression on instances, where each instance inherits its molecule's label. The molecule score is the max over its atoms of the instance logit, aggregated with a log-sum-exp (temperature 1) so that the score is smooth. Fit the instance model by gradient descent with L2 regularisation (lambda=1e-3) for 200 steps of full-batch L-BFGS via scipy.optimize.minimize with the EM-style re-assignment of the label-positive instances described as: keep only instances whose current logit is in the top 50% of each positive molecule. Rank-average the resulting molecule scores with the existing XGBoost members.
backlog.title: Atom-level multiple-instance model with max pooling

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed equal-weight rank average with a per-test-molecule weight. For each test molecule, compute its maximum Tanimoto similarity to the training set on Morgan bit vectors (radius 2, 2048 bits). Define the gate g = clip((sim_max - 0.3)/0.4, 0, 1). Final score = g * (average of XGBoost member ranks) + (1 - g) * (rank of the curated-descriptor random forest), so that molecules unlike the training set rely on the descriptor model, which generalises better across scaffolds. Rank-normalise the final scores to [0,1]. This only changes how the existing members are combined, so no new models need to be trained.
backlog.title: Similarity-gated member blending

backlog.spec: Add to featurize: BertzCT (Descriptors.BertzCT), the number of stereocentres found with Chem.FindMolChiralCenters(m, includeUnassigned=True), the number of fused ring systems (count of ring-system components from the RingInfo atom-ring sharing), the number of aromatic rings, and the fraction of heavy atoms that are sp2 carbons. Replace NaN or inf with 0. Append these five to the curated descriptor matrix. Complexity and stereocentre count track natural-product-like and peptidic compounds, which tend to penetrate the BBB less, and they are not captured by the existing ring-skeleton fingerprints.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped chemical complexity and stereochemistry features

backlog.spec: Instead of the fixed 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint, build the Morgan count fingerprint with unfolded identifiers (GetSparseCountFingerprint, radius 2). Keep only substructure identifiers that occur in at least 5 training molecules and at most 80% of them, then rank these by document frequency and keep the top 1024 as columns. Map test molecules onto the same column list (unseen identifiers are dropped). Train the existing XGBoost member on these columns and rank-average it with the other members. This is a data-driven vocabulary, so it adapts to the training set rather than relying on hash collisions.
backlog.title: Hashed Morgan count features with adaptive bit-budget by frequency

backlog.spec: Add a linear member trained to maximise pairwise ordering directly, which is what AUROC measures. Standardise the curated descriptors and the 2048-bit Morgan presence bits. Sample 200000 random (positive, negative) training pairs per fit (seeded). Minimise the mean logistic loss log(1+exp(-(s_pos - s_neg))) plus an L2 term 1e-3*||w||^2 with a linear score s = X w, using scipy.optimize.minimize (L-BFGS-B) on the pair-difference matrix in mini-batches of 20000 pairs, or with a single full-batch pass if memory permits. Convert the resulting scores to ranks and average them with the XGBoost members. The objective matches the metric, so it may reorder the decision boundary in ways a classification loss does not.
backlog.title: Pairwise-margin AUROC optimisation of a linear scorer

backlog.spec: Run the existing three-member XGBoost ensemble in two passes inside fit_predict. In pass one, fit each member normally and compute out-of-fold predictions on the training set with a 3-fold split that groups molecules by Murcko scaffold (GroupKFold, seeded shuffle). In pass two, refit each member with sample weights of 1 for the 70% of training molecules that were easiest to classify correctly and 2 for the 30% that were misclassified by their out-of-fold prediction (ranks above or below the class-prior threshold). Use the same hyperparameters. Rank-average the pass-two members for the test set. Only the training weights change, so the pipeline's structure is unaffected.
backlog.title: Two-pass hard-negative curriculum for the boosted members

backlog.spec: In fingerprints() and featurize(), standardize each molecule before any descriptor or fingerprint is computed: apply rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize Uncharger to neutralize charges, then TautomerEnumerator().Canonicalize(m) to pick a canonical tautomer. Keep the existing salt and largest-fragment handling. Wrap each step in try/except and fall back to the unstandardized molecule on failure. Everything downstream (Morgan, atom-pair, MACCS, curated descriptors, ACID and BASIC_AMINE SMARTS counts) is unchanged. The aim is that tautomer and ionization-form variants of the same compound map to identical features, which should help ranking on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Tautomer canonicalization and charge neutralization before featurization

backlog.spec: Extend featurize() with counts of structural alerts from rdkit.Chem.FilterCatalog. Build one FilterCatalog for each of PAINS, Brenk and NIH catalogs (FilterCatalogParams with the matching FilterCatalogs enum values). For each molecule, record the number of matching entries per catalog (3 numbers) and the number of distinct alert descriptions (3 numbers). Append these 6 columns to the existing 10 curated descriptors, so the descriptor matrix becomes 16 columns. Leave the fingerprint members and the XGBoost ensemble structure unchanged, and feed the descriptor matrix as an additional XGBoost member, replacing nothing else.
backlog.title: RDKit structural-alert counts as extra curated descriptors

backlog.spec: Swap the MACCS feature set in fingerprints() for the 42 molecular quantum numbers from rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_(m), which are integer counts of atom types, bond types, polarity and topology. Concatenate them with the 10 curated descriptors to form a 52-column dense matrix. Keep the same three-member XGBoost loop, so the Morgan and atom-pair members are untouched and the MACCS member becomes the MQN-plus-curated member. Keep max_features and the other hyperparameters the same, and use float32 arrays. Compare against the incumbent three-member average on the same 15 folds.
backlog.title: Molecular Quantum Numbers replace the MACCS member

backlog.spec: After the rank-averaged ensemble score is computed on the test set, compute each test molecule's mean Tanimoto similarity to its 5 nearest training molecules using 2048-bit Morgan bit vectors (use BulkTanimotoSimilarity). Convert it to an applicability weight w = clip((sim - 0.2)/0.4, 0, 1). Then shrink the normalized score toward the training base rate: final = w * score + (1 - w) * base_rate, where base_rate is the training mean of train_y mapped onto the same normalized scale. This pulls predictions for molecules far from the training chemistry toward the middle, so they stop competing confidently with in-domain molecules. All other pipeline steps are unchanged.
backlog.title: Applicability-domain shrinkage of test scores

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, standardize the 10 curated descriptors on the training set and run KMeans with k=4 (random_state=seed, n_init=10) on the training matrix. For each cluster, fit a shallow XGBoost (max_depth 3, 200 rounds, learning_rate 0.05, colsample_bytree 0.5) on the training molecules in that cluster, and also fit one global model on all training data using the existing three-feature-set ensemble. For each test molecule, assign it to its nearest cluster centroid, and blend its cluster-expert probability with the global ensemble probability using weight 0.5 each. Apply the rank normalization at the end as before. The idea is to capture regime-specific rules such as size-dependent polarity cutoffs without fragmenting the data too finely.
backlog.title: Local expert models over descriptor k-means clusters with global shrinkage

backlog.spec: Replace the final sum of per-member rankdata values in fit_predict with an aggregation in logit space. For each of the three XGBoost members, convert the predicted probability p to logit(clip(p, 1e-6, 1-1e-6)).
