Stack the three logit vectors for each test molecule and take the trimmed mean that drops the minimum and maximum values, which with three members means taking the median. Then pass the aggregated score through a sigmoid and apply the same min-max normalization as before. This is an aggregator change only: the three XGBoost fits, their features and hyperparameters stay identical, so the difference isolates the effect of robust combination.
backlog.title: Logit-space trimmed mean across ensemble members

backlog.spec: In fingerprints(), change the atom-pair member from raw counts to size-normalized log counts. Compute the count fingerprint with the existing atom-pair generator, divide each column by the number of heavy atoms of its molecule, and then apply log1p to the result. Scale the values by a constant (multiply by 100) so XGBoost's column sampling behaves the same as before. This removes the bias toward larger molecules in the raw count values, where big molecules have more pairs and more non-zero bins. The Morgan and MACCS members and the ensemble loop are otherwise unchanged.
backlog.title: Heavy-atom-normalized log-count atom-pair features

backlog.spec: Replace the default logistic objective in each XGBoost fingerprint member with a custom squared-hinge objective (the L2-SVM loss) passed through XGBoost's objective callable. Map labels to y in {-1, +1}. Compute margin m = y * f, where f is the raw margin output. Gradient for the loss max(0, 1 - m)^2 is -2 * y * max(0, 1 - m), and the Hessian is 2 * 1[m < 1] (clip the Hessian to a small positive floor such as 1e-3 for stability). At prediction time, convert the raw margin with a sigmoid to get a probability for rank averaging. Keep depth, rounds, learning rate and subsampling unchanged. The hinge loss focuses training on molecules near the decision boundary and may improve ordering in the middle of the score range.
backlog.title: Squared-hinge custom objective for the fingerprint boosters

backlog.spec: Compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold of each molecule with MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol. Build a side-chain-only molecule by deleting the scaffold atoms from the molecule with RWMol (keep atoms not in the scaffold match, and keep the attachment atoms as dummy atoms so the bond information is preserved). Compute 2048-bit Morgan radius-2 presence bits on this side-chain-only molecule, and use it in place of the full-molecule Morgan member in the three-feature-set XGBoost ensemble. Scaffold-containing bits then no longer dominate the representation, which may generalize better across unseen scaffolds, which is the evaluation setting. Handle acyclic molecules (empty scaffold) by using the full molecule.
backlog.title: Side-chain-only Morgan fingerprint replacing the full-molecule Morgan member

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, stack the training and test Morgan bit vectors. Build a kNN similarity graph over all molecules (k=10 nearest by Tanimoto, symmetrized, edge weights equal to the similarity). Compute the 16 smallest nontrivial eigenvectors of the normalized graph Laplacian with scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh (or dense numpy.linalg.eigh if the graph is small), using the seed for the initialization where applicable. Append these 16 embedding coordinates to the feature matrix of the Morgan member only, and fit the existing XGBoost model. Training labels are used only in the fit, not in the embedding, so the embedding is unsupervised and transductive; it encodes cluster structure that tree models cannot derive from raw bits.
backlog.title: Spectral embedding of the transductive Tanimoto graph as extra features

backlog.spec: Train two XGBoost members per feature set with different seeds and column subsamples. In each boosting stage, each member picks the 80% of training molecules with the lowest current logloss under the other member, and the next round of each member is fit only on the samples its peer selected. Use a fixed schedule that drops the kept fraction from 100% to 80% over the first 300 rounds, then holds it. Average the two members' rank scores at prediction time. This targets noisy or mislabelled BBB labels without a separate cleaning pass.
backlog.title: Co-teaching with small-loss sample selection

backlog.spec: Replace the tree members with kernel ridge regression on the 2048-bit atom-pair count vectors, using the MinMax (generalised Jaccard) kernel K(a,b)=sum_i min(a_i,b_i)/sum_i max(a_i,b_i), computed as a dense train-by-train matrix. Solve (K + lambda I) alpha = y_pm with lambda=1.0 via a Cholesky solve, where y_pm is the labels mapped to plus or minus one. Score test molecules by K_test @ alpha and return rank-normalised scores. The kernel is count-aware, unlike the binary Tanimoto SVC already tried, and needs no hyperparameter search beyond lambda.
backlog.title: MinMax-kernel ridge classifier on atom-pair counts

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a short genetic programme over expression trees built from the 10 curated descriptors (ops: +, -, *, safe divide, log1p, square, max, min; depth at most 3). Population 300, 25 generations, tournament selection, subtree crossover and mutation, fitness equal to inner 3-fold AUROC on the training molecules. Keep the best 5 expressions, add them as extra columns next to the curated descriptors, and fit one small XGBoost (depth 3, 300 rounds). Use seed for all randomness. Cap total runtime so each fit stays well under the 10-minute job limit.
backlog.title: Evolved descriptor formulas by small genetic programming

backlog.spec: Before fitting, standardise the curated descriptor matrix using training statistics. Then compute the test-set covariance and the training covariance, form the CORAL whitening-recolouring transform (whiten the test features with the test covariance, then recolour them with the training covariance), and apply it to the test descriptors only. Feed the aligned test descriptors to the existing XGBoost ensemble, keeping fingerprint inputs unchanged. Use a small ridge term of 1e-3 on each covariance to keep the matrices invertible. This adjusts for distribution shift between training and test skeleton families without using test labels.
backlog.title: CORAL-style transductive covariance alignment

backlog.spec: For each test molecule, build up to three views: the original, the stereo-stripped version, and the largest-fragment version with charges neutralised. Compute the same fingerprints and descriptors for every view with the same featurizer, pass each view through the trained ensemble, and average the three rank scores with weights 0.5, 0.25 and 0.25, falling back to the original view when the variant is identical or fails to parse. Training molecules keep their original features. The aim is to reduce sensitivity to salt, stereo and charge noise in the inputs at prediction time.
backlog.title: Test-time view averaging over parent-fragment variants

backlog.spec: Build a two-layer MLP on the 2048-bit Morgan presence bits (hidden 256, ReLU, dropout 0.3). Keep an exponential-moving-average copy of the weights (decay 0.99) as the teacher. Each minibatch, feed the student one view with random 20% bit dropout and the teacher a different view with 10% dropout. Loss is binary cross-entropy on labelled rows plus a consistency term, the mean squared difference between student and teacher sigmoid outputs, weighted by 1.0 after a 10-epoch ramp-up. Train for 60 epochs with Adam at lr 1e-3, batch 64. Return the EMA teacher's sigmoid output on test molecules, and rank-average it into the existing ensemble.
backlog.title: Mean-teacher MLP with bit-dropout consistency

backlog.spec: Define a small grid of 8 XGBoost settings varying max_depth (3, 5), learning_rate (0.03, 0.1) and colsample_bytree (0.2, 0.4). For each feature set, run a 4-fold inner split on the training molecules and compute each setting's out-of-fold mean logloss. Convert those losses to weights with softmax(-n * loss), with n equal to the number of inner-validation rows. Refit every setting on all training data and combine their test probabilities using these weights, before the usual rank averaging across feature sets. Use seed for all splits. The weights are chosen by likelihood, not by AUROC, so the averaging stays well calibrated.
backlog.title: Bayesian model averaging over a hyperparameter grid

backlog.spec: Before fitting the curated-descriptor member, apply SMOTE with k=5 nearest neighbours to the minority class (BBB-negative molecules) in the standardised 10-feature space, generating synthetic rows until the classes are balanced. Use the seed for the random interpolation. Fit the descriptor XGBoost on the augmented set and keep the fingerprint members trained on the original, unaugmented rows, since synthetic fingerprints are not meaningful. Average the descriptor member's rank with the others as before.
backlog.title: SMOTE oversampling in curated descriptor space

backlog.spec: For each XGBoost member, split the training molecules into an inner scaffold-grouped 80/20 holdout using seed-derived group assignments. Train with learning rate 0.1 for up to 600 rounds, evaluating inner logloss every 25 rounds. Whenever the inner logloss has not improved for 75 rounds, halve the learning rate and continue from the current booster via xgb_model. Stop when the learning rate falls below 0.00625. Refit the member on the full training set using the same schedule of rounds and learning rates. This adapts the step size to the data without fixing a round count in advance.
backlog.title: Learning-rate halving on an inner scaffold plateau

backlog.spec: Compute each training molecule's Murcko scaffold frequency across the training set. Assign sample weights proportional to the inverse square root of that frequency, multiplied by a class weight equal to the ratio of positive to negative training counts for the minority class, then normalise weights to mean 1. Pass them as sample_weight to all three XGBoost members. This combines rarity weighting with class balance, and differs from the earlier scaffold-family weighting by also correcting for label imbalance.
backlog.title: Fold-wise scaffold-rarity sample weighting for minority BBB-negatives

backlog.spec: Add a graph-kernel member. For each molecule, start from atom labels (atomic number, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, total H count) and run 3 Weisfeiler-Lehman refinement iterations: at each step relabel every atom by hashing its label together with the sorted labels of its neighbours. Count all labels from all iterations into one sparse count vector per molecule, with hashes folded into 4096 buckets. Build the linear kernel matrix from these count vectors, normalised by the square root of self-similarity. Fit SVC(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0) on the training kernel and take decision_function for test-vs-train rows. Rank-average this member with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight. Leave all other code unchanged.
backlog.title: Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree kernel SVM

backlog.spec: Add a local model member. For each test molecule, take the 150 most similar training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on the 2048-bit Morgan bits, weight them by similarity squared, and fit a weighted L2 logistic regression (C=0.3, max_iter=200) on the 10 curated descriptors, standardised using training statistics. The member's score is the local logistic probability for that test molecule. Average its ranks with the existing XGBoost member ranks at equal weight. Pass the seed as random_state wherever a solver accepts it.
backlog.title: Locally weighted logistic regression over Tanimoto neighbourhoods

backlog.spec: Add a sparse gated linear member on the concatenation of Morgan bits and MACCS keys. Learn a weight vector w and gate logits phi with Adam (lr 0.01, 600 steps, full batch, L2 penalty 1e-4 on w). In each step sample gates z from the hard-concrete distribution (beta=2/3, gamma=-0.1, zeta=1.1) using a numpy RandomState seeded from the seed argument, and use w times z in the logit. At prediction time use the deterministic expected gate. Rank-average this member with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight.
backlog.title: Hard-concrete L0-gated logistic regression trained with Adam

backlog.spec: Replace the single fit per feature set with 10 bags. For each bag, split the training molecules into an inner 80/20 split grouped by Murcko scaffold, using the seed to choose the split. Fit the XGBoost member on the 80 percent part and compute AUROC on the 20 percent part. Then refit on all training data for each bag, and combine the bags' test rank vectors with weights equal to max(inner AUROC minus 0.5, 0) normalised to sum to one. If all weights are zero, fall back to equal weights. Keep the three feature sets and the rank average across them.
backlog.title: Quality-weighted scaffold bagging by inner held-out AUROC

backlog.spec: Append 16 spectral-embedding coordinates to the curated descriptors. Build a symmetrised k=10 nearest-neighbour graph over all molecules (train plus test together, transductive) using Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bits. Compute the 16 smallest nontrivial eigenvectors of the normalised graph Laplacian, and use them as features. Fit ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=seed) on these features and rank-average it with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight. This recombines two previously helpful pieces and needs a replicate run to confirm.
backlog.title: Spectral embedding combined with ExtraTrees

backlog.spec: Before the final fit for each feature set, run successive halving over a small grid of 6 configurations: max_depth in {3,5,7} crossed with learning_rate in {0.03, 0.1}. Start each configuration with 100 rounds on a scaffold-grouped inner 75/25 split, then keep the top half by inner AUROC and double their rounds to 200, then keep the top configuration and train it for 500 rounds on all the training data. Use the chosen depth and learning rate for that feature set's member only. Seed all splits from the seed argument.
backlog.title: Successive halving over XGBoost depth and learning rate

backlog.spec: Add a fourth XGBoost member on a sparse random projection of the 2048-bit Morgan count vector to 256 dimensions. Build the projection matrix with sklearn SparseRandomProjection(n_components=256, density=1/3, random_state=seed), fitted on the training molecules only. Fit XGBoost with the same settings as the other members and rank-average it with them at equal weight. Its purpose is to add a dense, hashed view that differs from raw bit splits.
backlog.title: Sparse random projection member on Morgan counts

backlog.spec: Add a Bayesian linear member on the 10 curated descriptors plus the 2048-bit Morgan bits reduced by keeping only bits set in at least 5 training molecules. Fit MAP weights with a Gaussian prior of precision 1.0 using L-BFGS. Compute the Hessian at the MAP, invert it to get the posterior covariance, and form the posterior predictive logit for each test molecule as mean times variance-adjusted scaling: logit divided by sqrt(1 plus pi times predictive variance over 8). Use the adjusted probability as the member's score and rank-average it with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight.
backlog.title: Laplace-approximate Bayesian logistic regression with predictive variance

backlog.spec: Add a small neural network member: a single hidden layer of 64 ReLU units on Morgan count features (log1p transformed) plus the 10 curated descriptors standardised. Train with Adam (lr 1e-3, batch size 64, 60 epochs), gradient-norm clipping at 1.0, and weight decay 1e-4, using numpy only. Use the seed for initialisation and shuffling. Average the outputs of 3 such networks trained with different seeds derived from the seed argument, and rank-average the result with the existing XGBoost members at equal weight.
backlog.title: Clipped-gradient Adam fit of a shallow neural network on count features

backlog.spec: Before fitting each XGBoost member, replace each training label by a mix of its hard label and the mean label of its 5 nearest training neighbours by Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bits, computed within the training set only. Use target = 0.8 times the hard label plus 0.2 times the neighbour mean, and fit with XGBoost using the regression objective on these soft targets, so predictions are still probabilities. Rank-average the members as before.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-neighbour label smoothing of training targets

incumbent.description: Swap the RandomForest in the three-feature-set ensemble for XGBClassifier (500 trees, depth 5, lr 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.3, min_child_weight 2, logloss, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8), keeping the existing Morgan, atom-pair, and MACCS featurizers and rank-averaging.

memo: Helped: only large structural changes.
